_record_notice: Independent reviewer ruling on whether Plan 3 may be CLOSED. Produced by a reviewer who did not implement Plan 3 and who wrote no source, test, doc, ledger or other evidence artifact in the course of this review — this record is the only file written. The reviewer was asked to test the hypothesis that 'only the close record is missing, not the work', and was instructed to STOP and report rather than close if anything substantive turned out to be outstanding. Three substantive items are outstanding. This record therefore REFUSES the close and enumerates what must happen first.

verdict: REFUSED — Plan 3 may NOT be closed at 4bb9be3. The hypothesis under test ('only the paperwork is missing') is REFUTED, though narrowly and not on the science. The certification result, its evidence base, its sealed-label discipline and every condition raised by the five prior reviewer records are sound and discharged — that half of the hypothesis holds and is recorded below in full, so that a later close does not have to re-establish it. What refutes the hypothesis is three items that are work, not paperwork: (O1) two sections of the accepted Plan 3 were neither executed nor descoped, and no record says which; (O2) a claim carrying README, report and abstract surfaces attributes the headline loss to an error CATEGORY its evidence does not measure; (O3) a limitation that Plan 2's close explicitly carried forward is absent from the publication surfaces it was directed at. O2 and O3 are changes to the claim ledger, which CLAUDE.md requires an independent review for; O1 is a decision nobody has made. None of the three can be discharged by writing this file.

hypothesis_under_test.hypothesis: Plan 3 is executed and independently reviewed; what is missing is the close record, not the work.
hypothesis_under_test.what_the_evidence_supported: The execution half is fully supported. The certification run is legitimate and its artifact immutable; every diagnostic artifact reproduces byte-identically from committed commands under this reviewer's own re-run; the sealed splits are provably untouched; and all 5 prior records' conditions (1a/1d, three pre-conditions, A1-A4, C1-C4, R1-R7, P1-P5, Q1/Q2/Q4) are discharged. If the only question were 'is the certification result what it says it is', the answer is yes.
hypothesis_under_test.what_refuted_it: The close would have had to certify two things Plan 2's close standard requires and that this reviewer cannot certify at 4bb9be3: that no Plan 3 work was silently dropped (O1), and that no claim exceeds its evidence (O2, and O3 as an omitted limitation). Each of these is the specific failure mode the owner's instruction named, encountered rather than hypothesised.
what_would_have_changed_my_mind: On O1 — an ADR, or an amendment to ADR 0010, disposing of §11 and §12 the way ADR 0010 disposes of §9/§10 and ADR 0011 §3 disposes of the WikiEvents arm. I looked for one under every phrasing (render-report, Phase E, taxonomy, sensitivity, bootstrap, Spearman, AUROC, max-frame, strict loss) across docs/, src/ and evidence/, and searched the full evidence artifact inventory. There is none. Had ADR 0010's reasoning extended to §11/§12 on its own terms rather than resting entirely on 'there is no selected policy', I would have accepted it as covering them.

On O2 — a §12.1 machine-coded taxonomy over the certification split showing the content-bearing loss is dominated by in-role entity substitution, or a wording that stops at what the decomposition measures ('grounded, well-formed, content-bearing output that is wrong', which is what docs/plan3/certification-result.md line 91 actually says). Either would have closed it. I also tried to falsify my own objection by measuring, and the measurement did not fully vindicate either side — see O2's evidence block.

On O3 — the abstain/extract flip rate appearing in CX-SERVING-01's limitations, or in any publication surface, or a recorded ruling that Plan 3's infeasibility makes it moot. None exists; I grepped every doc, the README, the write-up draft, the generated claims appendix and the ledger.

standard_applied.text: Plan close requires the independent reviewer to reproduce the evidence base from committed commands, confirm the outstanding rulings, verify no token/restricted-data/sealed-label leakage, and confirm no claim exceeds its evidence. The plan's implementer may not complete the record.
standard_applied.how_it_bound_this_review: The first three limbs PASS and are recorded below. The fourth limb — no claim exceeds its evidence — FAILS on O2, and O3 is the same limb read as an omitted limitation. A fifth obligation is implicit in a close and is where O1 sits: a close asserts the plan's work is finished or deliberately dropped, and cannot be issued over sections whose disposition nobody has recorded.

O1_two_plan_sections_neither_executed_no.required_before_close: An ADR — or a dated amendment to ADR 0010 — that disposes of §11 and §12 item by item, separating what is moot for want of an accepted set, what is moot for want of an unsealed shift split, and what remains computable at $0 on already-open splits and is being dropped anyway with a stated reason. It must be independently reviewed, as ADR 0010 and ADR 0011 §3 were. Deciding to RUN the computable remainder is equally acceptable and would moot most of the ADR; that is the owner's and implementer's call, not the reviewer's.

O2_a_live_claim_attributes_an_error_cate.claim: CX-GROUNDING-ORTHOGONAL-01, evidence/plan4/claim_ledger.json. Surfaces: README, report, abstract.
O2_a_live_claim_attributes_an_error_cate.the_wording: '… because 87% of its remaining loss is grounded, well-formed, content-bearing output that names the wrong entity.'
O2_a_live_claim_attributes_an_error_cate.what_the_evidence_establishes: evidence/plan3/loss_decomposition.json establishes, exactly and against the certified quantity, that 0.530 of QA's 0.607 group-level loss (87.3%) sits in the valid-content-bearing channel, and that the within-channel mean loss is 0.579. That is a statement about WHERE the loss sits and HOW MUCH it is. It says nothing about WHICH of §12.1's error categories produced it — missing gold argument, extra grounded but incorrect argument, wrong role, boundary/normalisation mismatch, duplicate argument, or coreference/alias mismatch are all consistent with it.
O2_a_live_claim_attributes_an_error_cate.what_the_attribution_actually_rests_on: docs/adr/0007-plan3-certification-parameters-frozen.md lines 88-93: 'Manual inspection of high-loss valid QA documents shows the pattern clearly …' followed by two examples (victim 'Mrs. Clinton' vs 'she'; candidate 'Trump' vs 'dictators'). That is unquantified manual inspection, on the DEVELOPMENT split, from two instances. The accepted plan's §12.3 addresses this case by name: 'Use phrasing such as "associated with", "concentrated in" or "consistent with". Do not claim QLoRA caused a linguistic failure type from a few examples without a designed causal test.' The designed measurement is §12.1 — which is exactly the section O1 finds was never run and never dropped. The two findings are the same finding seen from two ends.

reviewer_measurement.purpose: I tried to falsify my own objection rather than assert it, by measuring whether the pattern is at least consistent with entity substitution. A substitution produces one false positive AND one false negative; a missing gold argument produces a false negative only; an extra argument produces a false positive only.
reviewer_measurement.method: For each system, every certification-split document in the valid-content-bearing channel, scored with conformalextract.evaluation.evaluate_document against RAMS gold, using the repository's own loaders (cli._reanalysis_inputs, predictions.parse_arm, reanalysis.loss_channel) and each system's frozen per-system confidence candidate. Run from a scratch directory; nothing was written into the repository.
reviewer_measurement.qa_certification_content_bearing: 2,847 documents, of which 332 score zero loss. tp 2,984 / fp 4,434 / fn 3,797. Of the 2,515 error-bearing documents, 2,003 (80%) carry BOTH a false positive and a false negative, 178 carry false negatives only, and 334 carry false positives only.
reviewer_measurement.baselines_for_context: ZS content-bearing: 1,238 documents, tp 32 / fp 1,319 / fn 2,765. FS: 1,130 documents, tp 110 / fp 1,135 / fn 2,636.
reviewer_measurement.what_this_does_and_does_not_settle: It PARTLY VINDICATES the attribution: at 80% of error-bearing documents the fp+fn signature is what substitution looks like, and 'mostly missing arguments' is ruled out. It does NOT settle it, in two ways. First, wrong-ROLE, boundary/normalisation and coreference/alias errors produce the identical fp+fn signature and are not 'naming the wrong entity' — separating them is precisely §12.1's job and it was not done. Second, false positives exceed false negatives by 637 arguments, i.e. the system systematically emits MORE arguments than gold contains. Over-generation is not an entity-naming error and the wording carries no trace of it. ADR 0007's own phrasing is narrower and better — 'in the right role, but names the wrong entity' — and a pure in-role substitution would keep fp and fn equal, which they are not.

O2_a_live_claim_attributes_an_error_cate.why_no_prior_reviewer_caught_it: Stated in fairness rather than as criticism. The reanalysis reviewer confirmed the 87% figure by from-scratch recomputation and ruled on this claim's wording twice (P3, then again in pass three) — but on the '0.000 for both baselines' qualifier, which is where the adversarial pressure was. The trailing clause was never the item under examination. This is the same pattern ADR 0012's Lesson records: a check that runs is not a check that bites, and the figure being right is not the same as the sentence being supported.
O2_a_live_claim_attributes_an_error_cate.required_before_close: Either narrow the wording to what the decomposition measures — docs/plan3/certification-result.md line 91 already has the defensible form, 'grounded, well-formed, content-bearing output that is simply wrong' — or run the §12.1 taxonomy and cite it. If the attribution is kept in any hedged form, §12.3's phrasing rule applies and the over-generation fact (fp exceeding fn by 637 arguments) belongs in the limitations. Because this is a claim-wording change, CLAUDE.md requires its own independent review; it may not ride along inside a close record. The same trailing clause appears at README.md line 68, docs/writeup/draft-2026-07-28.md line 109 and docs/writeup/claims-appendix.generated.md line 40, and all four must move together — the appendix is generated, so the ledger is the single upstream edit.

acceptance_rule: A plan close requires the independent reviewer to reproduce the evidence base from committed commands, confirm every outstanding ruling from every prior record, verify no token, restricted-data or sealed-label leakage, and confirm that no claim exceeds its evidence and that no planned work was dropped without a recorded, reviewed decision. A close record written to unblock a downstream gate is the artifact this repository exists to make impossible; where any limb fails, the correct output is this record and not a close. The Plan 3 implementer may not complete either this record or the close that supersedes it.
